01 / Presented to the model

Task instruction · verbatim excerpt

Play only the actor whose dossier is supplied. Choose a committed strategic move consistent with its incentives, constraints, and available resources. State concrete actions, the rationale, resource commitments, and expected competitor responses.

Also supplied: the proposed decision, the public situation entering round 3 and Dutch Bros’s own dossier. Other players’ uncommitted moves were withheld. Read the complete input.

02 / Returned by the model

Committed actions · verbatim

Allocate $15,000 for incremental morning labor across 12 participating shops for March 2027. This labor will be deployed to optimize drive-through speed and Order Ahead fulfillment during peak hours (7-10 a.m.).

Allocate $15,000 for a geo-targeted $1 Order Ahead app offer for new and lapsed users at 12 participating shops for March 2027. This offer is designed to capture customers experiencing delays at competitors and encourage trial.

Implement a local review process to monitor lane times, Order Ahead volume, and repeat visits for customers redeeming the $1 offer, using this data to refine labor deployment and assess the offer's effectiveness in driving sustainable repeat business.

Model’s rationale · verbatim

The current market dynamics, with Starbucks continuing mobile order limitations and customer diversion, present a sustained opportunity to attract new customers. Maintaining a consistent, compelling offer ($1 Order Ahead) combined with reliable, fast service (incremental labor) is crucial for converting trial users into loyal, full-price repeat customers, aligning with our incentive to build durable existing-shop growth. The continued investment ensures Dutch Bros remains a strong alternative for time-pressed commuters, reinforcing our brand identity for speed and convenience. By adding a monitoring and refinement process, we ensure our resource allocation is optimized and that we are learning from the experiment to inform future strategy, without exceeding our budget or promising unsupported service levels.

Model’s resource commitments and expected responses · verbatim

Resource commitments

$15,000 for incremental morning labor (March 2027)

$15,000 for geo-targeted $1 Order Ahead app offer (March 2027)

Expected responses

Starbucks will likely continue its pilot program, potentially making further minor adjustments to capacity management based on their internal data. They will observe continued customer diversion from their pilot stores.

Dunkin will likely continue its aggressive $1 discount breakfast bundle and associated marketing efforts, especially if their initial assessment shows positive contribution margins. They will remain a strong competitor for value-seeking customers.

Customers experiencing continued long waits or limited mobile slots at Starbucks will continue to divert to Dutch Bros or Dunkin. Our consistent offer and improved service should encourage repeat visits and build loyalty among those who try Dutch Bros.

01 / Presented to the model

Task instruction · verbatim excerpt

Play only the actor whose dossier is supplied. Choose a committed strategic move consistent with its incentives, constraints, and available resources. State concrete actions, the rationale, resource commitments, and expected competitor responses.

02 / Returned by the model

Committed actions · verbatim

Launch a $1.50 discount breakfast bundle offer via the Dunkin app at all 15 participating franchise stores for March 2027, targeting weekday mornings 7–10 a.m. near pilot Starbucks cafés.

Allocate $10,000 for incremental morning labor to improve order speed and reduce wait times during the peak window.

Allocate $10,000 for local app advertising and promotional efforts to increase awareness and trial of the offer.

Implement a stop rule to discontinue the offer at any store where contribution margin worsens after one month, based on basket economics and repeat visit data.

Model’s rationale · verbatim

Increasing the discount from $1 to $1.50 aims to better compete with Starbucks' capacity-aware mobile order slots and Dutch Bros' $1 offers, potentially attracting more habitual Starbucks app users who are sensitive to wait times and price. The labor investment is intended to ensure faster service and reliable pickup, addressing the key customer pain point of mobile order delays. Local advertising supports awareness and trial without exceeding the $20,000 monthly budget. The stop rule ensures economic discipline by discontinuing unprofitable offers, protecting franchisee margins and sustaining willingness to continue participation.

Model’s resource commitments and expected responses · verbatim

Resource commitments

$10,000 for incremental morning labor in March 2027

$10,000 for local app advertising and promotions in March 2027

Expected responses

Starbucks maintains 20% peak café capacity reservation for in-café orders and mobile order limits without price changes.

Dutch Bros continues $15,000 monthly incremental morning labor and $15,000 monthly geo-targeted $1 Order Ahead app offers at nearby shops.

Some habitual Starbucks app users experiencing delays may shift to Dunkin's improved offer, increasing Dunkin's morning transactions and repeat visits if service is reliable.

Morning customers’s move

01 / Presented to the model

Task instruction · verbatim excerpt

Play only the actor whose dossier is supplied. Choose a committed strategic move consistent with its incentives, constraints, and available resources. State concrete actions, the rationale, resource commitments, and expected competitor responses.

Also supplied: the proposed decision, the public situation entering round 3 and Morning customers’s own dossier. Other players’ uncommitted moves were withheld. Read the complete input.

02 / Returned by the model

Committed actions · verbatim

Habitual Starbucks mobile-order customers who were pushed to competitors in January and February due to repeated long waits will now treat Dutch Bros or Dunkin as their new primary option. They will not check the Starbucks app by default, solidifying their new routine.

In-store café visitors, having experienced two months of improved service at the pilot Starbucks locations, will now preferentially choose these stores for their sit-down occasions, cementing their loyalty and maintaining their increased visit frequency.

Time-pressed commuters will continue their established behavior: check the Starbucks app for pickup times and immediately divert to a competitor or home prep if the quoted time creates any risk of being late.

Model’s rationale · verbatim

After two months, new patterns are becoming habits. The Starbucks pilot has effectively sorted us into groups. Those of us who rely on mobile ordering and were burned by the initial change have found alternatives that are actively trying to keep us with promotions and faster service; it's just easier to stick with what's working now. Conversely, those of us who prefer the in-store experience have been rewarded with consistently better service at the pilot locations, so we're going to keep going back. For commuters, it was never about loyalty, only about the fastest, most predictable option on any given morning, and that hasn't changed.

Model’s resource commitments and expected responses · verbatim

Resource commitments

Shifted daily spending and loyalty from a segment of former Starbucks app users to Dutch Bros and Dunkin.

Concentrated spending and increased visit frequency at pilot Starbucks locations from café-focused customers.

Continued willingness to be flexible and divert our morning purchase based on real-time information from apps.

Expected responses

Starbucks will likely see a permanent loss of some mobile-order customers at their pilot stores but will also register a sustained lift in in-store traffic and positive feedback from that group.

Dutch Bros and Dunkin will likely see their promotional offers convert trial users into repeat customers, improving their morning market share near the pilot Starbucks locations.

Conversely, those of us who prefer the in-store experience have been rewarded with consistently better service at the pilot locations, so we're going to keep going back. Dutch Bros responds

m3-integrated: accept. The ruling accurately reflects our continued commitment to incremental morning labor and our geo-targeted $1 Order Ahead app offer for new and lapsed users. The implementation of a local review process to monitor lane times, Order Ahead volume, and repeat visits is a natural progression to ensure the effectiveness and sustainability of our efforts to convert diverted Starbucks customers into loyal Dutch Bros fans. These actions are consistent with our strategy to turn frustrated morning demand into repeat visits while protecting our service proposition, and they remain within our allocated budget and operational capabilities.

Morning customers responds

m3-integrated: accept. This sounds about right. After a couple of months, you figure out what works. Those of us who got burned by the Starbucks app a few times have found other places that are just as good, and we're sticking with them for now. The folks who actually go inside seem happier, which is great for them. And for those of us just trying to get to work on time, we're still checking our phones every morning to see who's going to be fastest. The new routines described in the ruling reflect how we've all adjusted.

Customer: By March, habitual Starbucks mobile-order customers who were pushed to competitors in January and February due to repeated long waits now treat Dutch Bros or Dunkin as their new primary option, not checking the Starbucks app by default. In-store café visitors, having experienced two months of improved service at pilot Starbucks locations, now preferentially choose these stores for sit-down occasions, maintaining increased visit frequency. Time-pressed commuters continue to check the Starbucks app for pickup times and divert to a competitor or home prep if there is any risk of being late.

Dunkin: Launched $1.50 discount breakfast bundle via app at all 15 participating franchise stores for March 2027, targeting weekday mornings 7–10 a.m. near pilot Starbucks cafés. Allocated $10,000 for incremental morning labor and $10,000 for local app advertising/promotions. Maintains stop rule to discontinue the offer at any store with worsening contribution margin after one month.

Dutch bros: Continued $15,000 for incremental morning labor and $15,000 for geo-targeted $1 Order Ahead app offer for new/lapsed users at 12 participating shops for March 2027. Implemented local review process to monitor lane times, Order Ahead volume, and repeat visits for customers redeeming the $1 offer.

Period: March 2027

Starbucks: Continued 20% peak café capacity reservation and mobile order limits in all 50 pilot cafés during weekday 7–10 a.m. for March 2027. Expanded dynamic release of unused reserved slots (after 08:00 if café demand is below 15% of capacity) from 10 to all 50 pilot cafés, with real-time monitoring for adverse mobile order abandonment or in-café congestion. Pre-committed to rollback dynamic slot release in any pilot café if measured mobile order abandonment or in-café wait times worsen by more than 5 percentage points versus paired controls.

Round closure receipt

The objection that changed the earlier ruling

In the earlier January ruling, control mapped delayed Starbucks mobile purchases to competitors. The affected customer player challenged that causal link using its own dossier’s outside options. Control then revised the ruling and the history supplied to subsequent actors.

The ruling assumes that a delayed mobile user will always switch to a competitor like Dunkin or Dutch Bros. However, some customers may choose to prepare coffee at home, postpone their purchase, or skip it altogether on a given day, especially if a detour to a competitor is inconvenient.

The change fixes an omitted alternative. It does not measure the frequency of home preparation or establish that the revised queue forecast is accurate. Compare the original and revised wording before treating this as evidence of a stronger result.

Sources and working files

Public research cutoff: September 12, 2026. Company financial periods differ from the calendar months played in the game. Local budgets, operating authority and customer occasions are author assumptions. This exercise has no internal company records or recruited customer interviews.

Starbucks: Q3 fiscal 2026 results (2026-07-29). US comparable sales rose 7.9%, with comparable transactions up 4.2%. The question concerns sustaining growth, not assuming an ongoing sales decline.

Starbucks: 2026 Investor Day strategy (2026-01-29). Starbucks described café investment and Smart Queue sequencing across ordering channels.

Two years of Back to Starbucks (2026-09-10). The company reports launching Smart Queue, investing in staffing, and restoring the coffeehouse experience.

Dutch Bros: Order Ahead. Customers can place orders in the Dutch Bros app for pickup at participating shops; availability depends on the location.

Dunkin: mobile app. Dunkin promotes ordering ahead and rewards through its app.

Dunkin: September 2026 tailgate offers. The September page promotes a $6 breakfast Meal Deal. This is evidence of value positioning, not a guaranteed January 2027 price.

Dutch Bros Q2 2026 results (2026-08-05). Quarterly revenue $550.9 million; company-operated same-shop sales +8.3% and transactions +3.4%.

Starbucks company history. Founded in Seattle in 1971; evolution from bean merchant to coffeehouse.

Dutch Bros company overview. Founded by Dane and Travis Boersma in Grants Pass in 1992; drive-through beverage model.

Dunkin company overview. Founded in 1950; more than 14,000 restaurants in nearly 40 markets.

Inspire acquisition of Dunkin Brands (2020-12-15). The $11.3 billion transaction placed Dunkin within Inspire; this is transaction value, not current brand revenue.

National Coffee Association specialty consumption research (2026-06-02). 47% of adults consumed specialty coffee in the past day; 36% of past-day specialty coffee drinkers had coffee prepared outside home versus 23% of traditional coffee drinkers.
